result:
I wrote the reply to `reply.txt` in the run folder.

The folder had four files. `FACTS.md` had the content. `prompt.txt` was the task. `session.json` and `session.err` were both empty, so there were no extra rules to follow beyond the prompt.

The reply is plain spoken prose. It says a standard DESIGN.md is a page of written rules, while her system backs the rules with one token file and checks on every build. It then gives the Round 2 results: 118 of 120 pages passed with the standard file, but with 30 button styles and 16 field styles. Her system passed 120 of 120, with 7 button styles and 4 field styles. It ends by pointing to the case study.

I spelled the numbers out as words so the text-to-speech engine reads them cleanly. The eval's "Spoken replies rules" in `DESIGN.md` weren't in this folder, so I couldn't check the reply against them.
